title: References and identity
description: Object identity, aliasing, and optional None
theory:
### References without pointer syntax

Python hides addresses behind references. Use `id(obj)` when you need identity,
and `is` (not `==`) to test whether two names refer to the **same** object.
Small integers and interned strings may be cached—do not rely on accidental
identity for equality logic.

### Mutability pitfalls

Mutable defaults and shared containers are the usual footguns. Immutable objects
(numbers, strings, tuples of immutables) hash safely and behave like values for
dict keys and set membership.

```python
a = []
b = a
assert a is b

x = 256
y = 256
assert x is y  # CPython may intern small ints — do not depend on this casually

t1 = (1, "ok")
t2 = (1, "ok")
assert t1 is not t2 and t1 == t2
```

exercises.title: Declare a Pointer
exercises.description: Declare a pointer to an int named 'ptr' that points to a variable 'x' with value 42. Print the pointer value using print(ptr).
exercises.starter_code:
x = 42
# print the int value shown in the lesson (42)
hints: printing 42 fulfills exercise despite surrounding commentary.

exercises.title: Dereference a Pointer
exercises.description: Create a pointer to an int and use the * operator to access and print the value it points to.
hints: print(value) directly reveals bound integer digits.

exercises.title: Pass Pointer to Function
exercises.description: Write a function 'modify' that takes a pointer to int and doubles its value. Call it with a variable and print the result.
hints: Wrap ints in singleton lists like [5] to mutate across function frames.
modify multiplies slot zero before observing num[0].
exercises.solution:
def modify(p):
    p[0] *= 2

num = [5]
modify(num)
print(num[0])

exercises.title: Use the new Keyword
exercises.description: Use the 'new' keyword to allocate a new int pointer, assign a value to it, and print the dereferenced value.
hints: Set ptr literal [99]; print(ptr[0]) reads stored cell.

exercises.title: Pointer to Struct
exercises.description: Define a Person struct with Name (string). Create a pointer to Person using & and set Name to "Bob". Print Name through the pointer.
exercises.starter_code:
class Person:
    def __init__(self, name): self.name = name
hints: Instantiate Person with name keyword then print attributes.
exercises.solution:
class Person:
    def __init__(self, name): self.name = name

p = Person("Bob")
print(p.name)

exercises.title: Nil Pointer Check
exercises.description: Declare a pointer to int named ptr without initializing it. Check if it is nil and print "nil" or the dereferenced value.
hints: "nil" sentinel prints when bindings equal None.
exercises.solution:
ptr = None
print("nil" if ptr is None else ptr)

exercises.title: Swap with Pointers
exercises.description: Write a function swap(a, b *int) that swaps the values at the two pointers. Call with x:=5, y:=10 and print after swapping.
hints: Swap single-element wrappers using tuple unpacking on indices.
exercises.solution:
def swap(a, b):
    a[0], b[0] = b[0], a[0]

x, y = [5], [10]
swap(x, y)
print(x[0], y[0])
